title: Request-shape-aware readiness scoring and regional failover gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current readiness/liveness probes are static and do not reflect the diversity of production requests. Heavy tail request shapes (long sequences, tool calls, high embedding batch sizes) can cause local probe success while real traffic experiences degraded latency or error rates. This leads to noisy autoscaler decisions, poor multi-region failover choices, and SLO regressions during load spikes.

Goal: Implement a request-shape-aware readiness scoring system and a regional failover gating mechanism that uses weighted probe signals tied to recent request distributions. The system should stabilize autoscaling decisions, reduce unnecessary load shedding, and ensure SLOs (P95 latency and availability) are respected during region-level incidents and scale events.
acceptance_criteria: Readiness score produced per serving pool every 10s combining probe outcomes and sampled production telemetry
Score calculation accounts for request shape buckets (short chat, long chat, embeddings, rerank) with configurable weights
Regional failover gate evaluates pools against headroom and readiness score before initiating cross-region shift
Autoscaler uses readiness-adjusted capacity signals; scale-down suppressions reduced by >=40% in 2-week canary versus baseline
End-to-end testbench demonstrates no more than 5% increase in P99 latency during synthetic long-sequence spike compared to baseline and improves availability during node failures
Dashboard and alerting for readiness delta, gate trigger counts, and per-route health breakdown are live in Console QA workspace
Documentation and runbook updated with rollback steps and experiment flags
design_decisions: Use sampled real-traffic headers to classify request shapes; default buckets: short (<=128 tokens), medium (129-1024), long (>1024), embeddings, rerank
Readiness score = weighted exponential moving average of (probe_pass_rate_by_bucket * bucket_weight * recent_error_penalty)
Probe bundle: synthetic prefix-based probes per pool + lightweight sampled production trace checks (latency & error thresholds) to surface degradation not visible to synthetic probes
Regional gate policy: require readiness_score >= threshold AND headroom >= min_capacity before shifting >10% of traffic to region; otherwise route to secondary with gradual canary
Autoscaler integration: readiness_score multiplies capacity_safety_factor to inhibit aggressive scale-downs during observed instability
Trade-off: sampled production checks introduce noise and modest cost; mitigated by sampling at 0.5% by default and priority-based increase for critical customers
Security: sampled traces strip PII and full content; only metadata (route, seq_len, status_code, latency) is evaluated
tasks: Implement request classification header propagation in API gateway - ENG Infra
Add sampled telemetry collector and bucket aggregator in runtime health pipeline
Implement readiness scoring service and persist per-pool time-series
Hook readiness score into autoscaler decision loop (scale-down gating) and into regional failover controller
Create console dashboard panels and alerts (QA workspace)
E2E canary deployment on staging with traffic replay harness
Load test and chaos scenarios (node kill, network partition) and record SLO metrics
Docs, runbook, and rollout feature flags
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged implementation in staging; 2) Canary in us-west-2 on non-critical pools with 2-week observation; 3) Expand to multi-pool in region and enable autoscaler gating; 4) Soft-enable regional gate for cross-region failover (observe but do not alter routing) for 3 days; 5) Fully enable gating for low-risk customers; 6) Gradual ramp to all regions. Rollback: flip FF off or set thresholds to conservative defaults; runbook lists immediate steps to revert autoscaler hooks and regional controller behavior.
test_plan: Unit tests for scorer math and edge cases, integration tests for header propagation and aggregator, staging canary with traffic replay that includes long-sequence, embeddings, and rerank scenarios. Chaos tests: kill 2 GPUs in a pool, saturate KV cache, induce elevated error-rate for a bucket. Success criteria: autoscaler does not oscillate; readiness score correctly reflects injected failures; regional gate prevents unsafe failover; SLOs measured against baseline in the canary are improved or within tolerance.
